title: Event Lifecycle and Data Exchange
readerIntent: Follow registration, publication, distribution, retry, and import/export interactions.
priorKnowledge: Know the delivery model and event owner.
owner: Publisher, event runtime, configured transport, NEMS, and consumer
summary: Nodics loads listener contracts, publishes a context-rich fact, delivers locally or remotely, persists state where configured, and records safe outcomes and recovery state.

sections.heading: Lifecycle
items: Load and merge source-owned listener definitions.
Resolve active module, tenant, and runtime context.
Publish a stable event type and version after the authoritative state transition.
Execute eligible local listeners and/or dispatch through the configured transport.
Persist distribution and event-log state when NEMS delivery is selected.
Acknowledge success or record bounded retry and manual-recovery evidence.
Refresh listener state through governed update/removal behavior.

sections.heading: Import interaction
paragraphs: A finalized import may publish completion or record-level facts after governed persistence succeeds. Consumers must be idempotent because retries or resumed imports can repeat delivery. Events must not create a direct persistence route that bypasses import validation and run history.

sections.heading: Export interaction
paragraphs: An export may be triggered by an event or publish a completion fact, but the event carries a governed reference and outcome rather than unrestricted exported data. Delivery providers do not replace export access policy, retention, checksum, or destination governance.
